findings.claim: The committed 'immutable' refiner history trail contradicts the packet's own archived review evidence: the 2026-08-29_20-20-25Z snapshot contains only state.json plus three checkpoints, while the archived round-2 verdict proves that snapshot also held decisions.md, refinement_log.md, and reflection.json, and the archived round-3 verdict cites a 2026-08-29_20-32-27Z history entry that is entirely absent from the change manifest.
findings.evidence: files.txt lists exactly four files under .refiner/history/v3-devtools-time-travel-archive-qa/2026-08-29_20-20-25Z/ (state.json, checkpoints/45bed4e9.json, checkpoints/9100ef56.json, checkpoints/f0578e81.json) and no other history entries, and the diff shows all four as new files — so nothing else was committed there. But round-2-findings.json states 'the same snapshot's decisions.md, refinement_log.md, and reflection.json retain the pre-correction round-1 text', and round-3-findings.json states '(and f0578e81.json, 9100ef56.json, and the 2026-08-29_20-32-27Z history copies)'. resolution.md claims the snapshot was restored to 'its original ... bytes' and reflection.json claims 'all five blocking constraints pass with exact evidence traceability' for the blocking evidence-and-fixture-integrity constraint — a claim the committed trail cannot support when files referenced by the retained verdicts are missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the complete 20-20-25Z snapshot contents (decisions.md, refinement_log.md, reflection.json, artifact_manifest.json, and the specify/plan checkpoints eca985ff/cb625bae) and the 20-26-47Z/20-32-27Z history entries the round-2/round-3 dispositions and findings reference, or amend resolution.md/reflection.json to state precisely which history files were never committed and why the archived verdicts describe files the repository does not contain.

findings.claim: The corrective plan's key premise is unverified: it assumes a signed end-task will 'regenerate projections' into a correct state, but the only demonstrated signed-API behavior toward this change is a 409 refusal to reopen a terminal Complete, and the already-consumed global counters (implementationCompleted 35, changes_completed 3, position.json done 35/63, status COMPLETE with tasks_done 6/10) have no shown signed path to be decremented — so the falsified projection may survive archive even if the post-gate sequence executes exactly as written.
findings.evidence: control-plane-correction.json records '"terminalReopenAttempt": "rejected-409"' and a postGateSequence of 'run signed end-task to complete task 10 and regenerate projections', yet the diff still ships progress.json with '"implementation_status": "COMPLETE"', '"status": "DONE"', '"tasks_done": 6' of 10, '"changes_completed": 3', and the stale '"next_task_pending": "Add targeted multi-store, retention, stale cursor, rewind/live, mutation ordering, import, and compatibility tests."' (contradicting the acceptance criterion 'do not add or run unit, isolated, mock-backed, snapshot, or partial tests'), plus position.json '"status": "COMPLETE"' with progress done 35/63. Nothing in the packet demonstrates that regenerating projections from a canonical state in which the change is already terminally Complete will produce anything other than the same false DONE record.
findings.suggested_fix: Before archive, dry-run or otherwise evidence what signed end-task actually writes to progress.json/position.json/current-waypoint.json for a change already in terminal Complete state; if it cannot correct the counters/status, record the uncorrectable falsification as a control-plane defect in the phase postmortem (the round-3 judge's alternative branch) rather than asserting end-task regeneration as the correction.

findings.claim: A file named rejection.md contains an anti-sycophancy PASS line with no round attribution, so it is ambiguous which of the four review rounds (three BLOCK verdicts plus the pending round-4 gate) this screen result belongs to.
findings.evidence: The single-line hunk is '[adv-gate] PASS (score=0.0803571417927742, strictness=strict)' in a file called rejection.md, while findings.json, round-2-findings.json, and round-3-findings.json all record '"verdict": "BLOCK"' and resolution.md describes a separate 'Round 4 gate' that 'must ... pass the strict anti-sycophancy screen'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the file to reflect its content (e.g., sycophancy-screen.md) and record per-round screen results with round identifiers, or add a header line naming the round this PASS covers.

findings.claim: current-waypoint.json holds '"currentTask": null' while control-plane-correction.json and the evidence README assert task 10 is in_progress and position-reminder.txt instructs agents to run '/kbd-apply v3-devtools-time-travel' as their first action, leaving the authoritative runtime file internally ambiguous about what work is active.
findings.evidence: The current-waypoint.json hunk shows '"currentTask": null' alongside '"exactNextCommand": "/kbd-apply v3-devtools-time-travel"', while control-plane-correction.json records '"task": { "id": "10", "status": "in_progress" }' and the evidence README states 'Canonical runtime state at revision 341 has phase in_progress and task 10 in_progress.'
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm whether the signed runtime should populate currentTask with task 10 at activation revision 341; if null is correct for a review-gate state, note that in the evidence README so auditors do not read currentTask: null as contradicting the in_progress task claim.
